title: Opera Omnia I (Delarue-Lommatzsch)
shelf_note: A 19th-century Latin edition of Origen (Lommatzsch reprint of Delarue). It fits a general European-libraries collection.
structure_note: printed_repeats 620 of 1,081 numbered pages, with 125 backsteps, is far more than misread numerals would produce. It suggests the printed pagination restarts, i.e. more than one printed volume in one scan. This leaf is 'ORIGENIS IN MATTHAEUM' p. 312, the Latin Commentariorum series (section 60), at record 807. As far as I recall, Lommatzsch's vol. I (1831) holds the John commentary, so the title 'Vol. 1' and the date 1834 may not describe this part of the scan. I have not confirmed this. Separately, structure.pages_translated is 0 while the pages_translated field is 1300, so the counts disagree (E2).

missing.english: M. and R. in the text: "but the day is at hand"; R., however, in the notes: "Manuscripts etc."
missing.why: 'M.' and 'R.' are the sigla for the earlier editions (Merlin and, presumably, Delarue/Ruaeus). A general reader cannot tell what they stand for.

missing.english: Merlin's editions: "whose lamp has thus been lit."
missing.why: Nothing says who Merlin is (the early 16th-century editor of Origen's Latin works), or why his reading is cited

book_verdict: The page is a clean single-column Lommatzsch leaf, but a dark blot over the right edge causes several unmarked garbles and omissions in the OCR, one of which reverses a sentence's sense in the transcription. The translation recovers sensibly, flagging its reconstructions with <unclear>, and its notes are mostly sound. The volume title and the many repeated printed page numbers deserve a check for concatenated volumes.
